newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica sets employee stock option plan.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica sets employee stock option plan.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp said on Tuesday it implemented an employee stock option plan allowing more than 85,000 BankAmerica employees to purchase between 50 and 90 shares of stock every six months over the next three years.

"Beginning today, tellers, teleservices representatives, loan officers -- indeed, most of our employees -- have a greater stake in the future of our company," Chairman and Chief Executive Officer David Coulter said.
A company spokesman said BankAmerica employs a total of about 92,700 people worldwide.
In the third quarter of 1996, BankAmerica reported earnings of $683 million, or $1.75 a share versus $704 million or $1.72 a share a year earlier.
As of the end of the third quarter, there was a total of 358 million common shares outstanding.
A BankAmerica spokesman said that NationsBank and Chase Manhattan have offered stock option award programs to employees in the past.
BankAmerica in the past year has been taking a hard look at all of its businesses to determine which units are producing adequate returns on capital, analysts said.
"This goes along with moves in BankAmerica, which is restructuring its retail operations," said one analyst.

"We're talking about a company getting more aligned in terms of having employees being shareholders and determining their own destinies in terms of impacts they can make on a company and their own wealth," the analyst said.
BankAmerica added that after three years, its board will review the stock option program and it will either be modified, extended or ended.
